# Adjudication Task — Chapter 341

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃341화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|며칠 전, 문경과 나누었던 대화가 뇌리를 스쳤다.
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|‘그동안 감사했습니다.’
 10|
 11|‘감사 인사는 무슨. 훌륭한 의원이 되는 것에만 집중해.’
 12|
 13|‘신의처럼요?’
 14|
 15|‘그래, 신의처럼.’
 16|
 17|
 18|
 19|그리고 지나치듯 흘린 마지막 한마디도.
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|‘아쉽지만 이번에는 함께 못 가겠네요. 이만 스승님께 돌아가야 해서요.’
 24|
 25|
 26|
 27|왜 몰랐을까.
 28|
 29|생각해 보면 문경은 처음부터 비범한 구석이 있는 녀석이었다. 수적들에게 목숨을 위협받는 상황에서 발휘한 놀라운 기지, 나이답지 않은 침착성과 뛰어난 의술까지.
 30|
 31|‘그뿐만이 아니야.’
 32|
 33|수적들에 의해 장강 밑바닥으로 가라앉을 뻔한 녀석이 넉살 좋게 쾌조선에 얻어 타지를 않나, 무림에서도 한 성깔 하기로 유명한 사천당문에 고작 약방문을 얻으러 갔다.
 34|
 35|간덩이에 보톡스를 맞은 무림인들도 꺼릴 법한 일들을, 문경은 아무렇지 않게 해 왔다.
 36|
 37|‘게다가 방금 보여 준 말과 행동들은…….’
 38|
 39|문경이 말한 흑수인(黑手印)이 어떤 무공이고 어느 정도의 위력을 지녔는지, 나는 모른다.
 40|
 41|다만 한 가지는 사실은 알겠다.
 42|
 43|“신의. 네가 바로 신의의 제자였어.”
 44|
 45|“……!”
 46|
 47|“……!”
 48|
 49|기쁨과 허탈함이 뒤섞인 내 말을 들은 다른 녀석들이 눈을 크게 뜨고 문경을 바라보았다.
 50|
 51|순간 내려앉은 숨 막히는 적막에 문경이 몸을 움츠렸다.
 52|
 53|“죄, 죄송해요. 하지만 말씀드릴 수 없었어요.”
 54|
 55|“어째서?”
 56|
 57|반사적으로 되묻고도 아차 싶었다. 일평생 정체를 숨기며 살아온 신의다. 그 제자인 문경이 입을 다문 것은 당연했다.
 58|
 59|아마도 묘령사태의 목숨이 경각에 달리지 않았다면, 녀석은 끝끝내 스승의 정체를 발설하지 않았을 것이 분명했다.
 60|
 61|“신의는, 아니 네 스승님께서는 지금 어디 계시지?”
 62|
 63|머뭇거리던 문경이 입술을 꼭 깨물었다.
 64|
 65|“그 전에, 한 가지만 약속해 주실 수 있나요?”
 66|
 67|“비밀은 지킨다. 반드시.”
 68|
 69|나는 단호한 대답과 함께 품에서 뭔가를 꺼내 보여 주었다.
 70|
 71|그건 요즘 들어 틈만 나면 인벤토리에서 꺼내 들여다보는 물건이었다.
 72|
 73|
 74|
 75|[오배자(五倍子)는 사천 땅에서 나는 것이 제일이오.]
 76|
 77|
 78|
 79|옥빛 사금파리에 적힌 희미한 글씨를 본 문경의 눈이 커다래졌다.
 80|
 81|“이건…….”
 82|
 83|“알아보겠어?”
 84|
 85|“네, 틀림없이 스승님의 필체인걸요.”
 86|
 87|신기한 듯 [신의의 증표]를 요모조모 살피던 문경이 아, 하고 탄성을 흘렸다.
 88|
 89|“그러고 보니 언젠가 스승님께서 그러셨어요. 아주 오래전, 어느 명의에게 사천으로 찾아오라는 증표를 남기신 적이 있다고. 그런데 어찌 이것을 공자님께서…….”
 90|
 91|“그 명의에게 직접 건네받았어. 신의가 아니면 치료할 수 없는 환자가 있거든.”
 92|
 93|나는 힘주어 말을 이었다.
 94|
 95|“반드시 살려야 하는 사람이야.”
 96|
 97|“어디의 누구신지는 모르나…… 공자님께서는 그분을 소중하게 여기시는군요.”
 98|
 99|소중한 사람이라.
100|
101|그래, 그런 것 같다. 내게 있어 적천강은 소중한 사람이다. 그는 나를 위해 모든 것을 내어 주었고, 이제는 내가 그를 지킬 차례다.
102|
103|“응. 맞아.”
104|
105|문경은 희미하게 웃으며 고개를 끄덕였다.
106|
107|“따라오세요. 스승님께 안내해 드릴게요.”
108|
109|
110|
111|* * *
112|
113|
114|
115|뽀득, 뽀드득.
116|
117|쌓인 눈이 걸음을 옮길 때마다 뭉개졌다.
118|
119|나는 주위를 둘러봤다. 서리 낀 앙상한 나뭇가지. 시선이 닿는 곳마다 소복하게 쌓인 새하얀 눈.
120|
121|‘봐도 봐도 신기하네.’
122|
123|밖은 새싹이 고개를 내미는 초봄인데, 지금 우리가 걷고 있는 곳은 눈 내린 어느 겨울날의 풍경이다.
124|
125|‘이게 바로 기문진(奇門陣)…….’
126|
127|신의에게 안내해 주겠다며 문경이 향한 곳은, 앞서 청성파와 함께 수색하던 바로 그 산이었다. 하지만 어느 지점에 이르러 그가 몇 개의 바위를 낑낑거리며 옮기니 새로운 길과 풍경이 펼쳐지는 것이 아닌가.
128|
129|‘난생처음 보는 광경에 나를 포함한 모두의 입이 딱 벌어졌었지.’
130|
131|문경은 이걸 설치해 준 사람이 기환노사(奇幻老師)라고 말해 줬다.
132|
133|궁기방이 침까지 튀겨 가며 설명한 바로는, 기환노사는 까마득한 과거에 천하제일의 진법가라 불리던 인물이라고 했다.
134|
135|그가 신의와 어떤 인연이 있었는지는 모르겠지만 이런 걸 설치해 놓다니. 하마터면 코앞에 두고 한참을 헤맬 뻔했다.
136|
137|‘이러니까 아무도 못 찾지.’
138|
139|날고 긴다는 무림인과 수많은 관군을 풀어놓으면 뭐 하나.
140|
141|정석대로 산 하나하나를 뒤졌다면 반년이 아니라 반세기로도 시간이 부족했을 것이다.
142|
143|“와아, 와아아!”
144|
145|눈밭에 풀어놓은 강아지처럼 몇 발짝 앞에서 뛰어가던 청풍이 탄성을 내질렀다. 뭐라 핀잔을 주려던 나도 다음 순간 완전히 뒤바뀐 광경에 입을 딱 벌렸다.
146|
147|“……와, 씨. 뭐냐 이거.”
148|
149|고작 몇 걸음 만에 또 세상이 바뀌었다.
150|
151|눈으로 온통 새하얗던 한겨울의 풍경이 아닌 완연한 봄으로.
152|
153|사방이 온통 푸르렀고 이름 모를 꽃들이 활짝 만개해 있었다. 넋 나간 얼굴로 다가온 혁무진이 물었다.
154|
155|“조장님. 지금 제가 헛것을 보고 있는 겁니까?”
156|
157|“나도 몰라, 인마.”
158|
159|우리 중 가장 무림 경험이 풍부한 궁기방조차도 멍하니 입을 벌린 채 중얼거렸다.
160|
161|“허어…… 헙! 퉷퉷! 이거 뭐야!”
162|
163|“나비?”
164|
165|세상에, 진짜 나비네. 그것도 한두 마리가 아니다.
166|
167|형형색색(形形色色).
168|
169|꽃밭 곳곳에 앉아 있던 수백 마리의 나비가 동시에 날아오르는 모습은 장관 그 자체였다.
170|
171|쏴아아아아.
172|
173|때마침 불어오는 바람은 어디에서 왔는지, 환하게 내리쬐는 햇살은 또 어디서 들어오는지.
174|
175|내게는 지금 보이는 하나하나가 7대 불가사의였다.
176|
177|‘여기에 비하면 피라미드는 아무것도 아니네.’
178|
179|몇 걸음 차이로 계절이 바뀌는 곳도 있는데 피라미드가 대수냐. 이집트 행정 보급관이 애들 굴려서 지었겠지 뭐.
180|
181|파라오가 근엄한 얼굴로 본 파라오는 너희에게 실망했다, 몇 번 날려 주면 채찍 맞으면서 돌 나르게 되어 있다.
182|
183|하지만 이곳은…… 완전히 다른 영역이다.
184|
185|“진 공자님?”
186|
187|“어? 어, 응.”
188|
189|“거의 다 도착했어요. 이제 저 언덕만 넘어가면 됩니다.”
190|
191|황급히 정신을 차린 우리는 문경을 따라 다시 걸음을 옮겼다.
192|
193|푸른 잔디로 뒤덮인 야트막한 언덕을 넘어서자, 평평한 대지에 홀로 서 있는 자그마한 모옥(茅屋) 한 채가 눈에 들어왔다.
194|
195|그리고…… 그곳에 ‘그’가 있었다.
196|
197|“스승님!”
198|
199|문경의 외침에 모옥 앞 텃밭에서 뭔가를 심고 있던 노인이 구부정한 허리를 폈다. 오는 길에 봤던 눈만큼이나 새하얀 수염. 주름진 눈매와 투명한 눈동자.
200|
201|우리를 발견했는지 노인의 눈매가 부드럽게 휘어졌다.
202|
203|“귀한 손님이 오셨구려.”
204|
205|드디어 찾았다. 신의(神醫).
206|
207|
208|
209|* * *
210|
211|
212|
213|신의와 제대로 대화를 나누게 된 것은 한참 후였다.
214|
215|묘령사태의 상태를 본 신의는 문경을 시켜 환자를 모옥으로 옮기게 했고, 두 사람이 다시 모습을 드러낸 것은 한 시진이 흐른 뒤였다.
216|
217|“오랜만이오. 누군가 찾아온 것은.”
218|
219|불쑥 들려온 신의의 목소리는 선선한 봄바람을 닮았다. 모옥 주변을 서성거리던 나는 황급히 허리를 숙였다.
220|
221|“태원 진가의 진태경이 신의를 뵙습니다.”
222|
223|“동봉(董奉).”
224|
225|“네?”
226|
227|“내 이름이오. 신의라는 별호는 과분하니 동 노인이라 불러 주시구려.”
228|
229|복덕방 김 영감도 아니고, 내가 천하의 신의에게 어떻게 동 노인이라고 부르겠나.
230|
231|‘심지어 나이도 손자뻘인데.’
232|
233|하지만 신의의 인자한 눈빛을 마주하고 있으니 잠자코 순응할 수밖에 없었다.
234|
235|“예. 그리하겠습니다. 동 노인.”
236|
237|“고맙소, 진 공자.”
238|
239|내 대답에 부드럽게 웃어 보인 신의는 그 뒤로도 한 사람, 한 사람과 인사를 주고받았다.
240|
241|그는 까마득하게 어린 우리에게도 예의를 지켰고 결코 서두르는 법이 없었다.
242|
243|“안녕하세요! 저는 청풍이에요!”
244|
245|이 구역의 미친놈 앞에서도 웃음을 잃지 않았다.
246|
247|“허허, 기운이 넘치는 분이군. 나는 동봉이라고 하오. 다른 분들처럼 동 노인이라 부르면 되오.”
248|
249|“저어, 하지만 할아버지가 어른들께는 예의를 차려야 한다고 하셨어요.”
250|
251|“조부께서 훌륭한 가르침을 내려 주셨구려. 하나 서로 마음만 맞는다면 무엇이 문제겠소. 그저 조금 나이 든 벗이 생겼다고 생각하시오.”
252|
253|“벗이요?”
254|
255|“그렇소, 벗.”
256|
257|청풍이 환하게 웃었다.
258|
259|“그럼 잘 부탁해. 동 노인!”
260|
261|“허허, 허허허!”
262|
263|이걸 웃어?
264|
265|무림의 조커인가? 화나도 웃고 어이없어도 웃는 뭐 그런.
266|
267|“동 노인은 당과 먹어 봤어?”
268|
269|“좋아한다오. 한때는 빙당호로도 즐겨 먹었었지.”
270|
271|“야, 나두!”
272|
273|배경은 힐링 영화인데, 대화 내용은 공포 스릴러가 따로 없다. 결국 얼굴이 새파랗게 질린 궁기방이 청풍의 주둥이를 두 손으로 꽉 막고 슬금슬금 물러났다.
274|
275|그 모습을 보며 껄껄 웃은 신의가 문경에게로 고개를 돌렸다.
276|
277|“재미있는 분들을 모셔 왔구나.”
278|
279|문경이 깊게 고개를 숙였다.
280|
281|“죄송합니다. 스승님의 허락도 없이.”
282|
283|“아니, 아니다. 인연은 하늘이 맺어 주는 것. 이 또한 순리겠지. 안 그렇소?”
284|
285|마지막 질문은 날 향한 것이었다. 고개를 끄덕인 나는 미리 준비해 둔 [신의의 증표]를 꺼내 내밀었다.
286|
287|“이것은…….”
288|
289|“오래전 신의, 아니 동 노인께서 남기신 증표입니다. 낙양괴의께서 이것을 주시며 찾아가라 하셨습니다.”
290|
291|“내가 말이오?”
292|
293|“예?”
294|
295|아니, 설마 이걸 까먹었나.
296|
297|잠시 고개를 갸웃거리던 신의는 문경이 재차 일깨워 주고 난 후에야 탄성을 흘렸다.
298|
299|“아아, 그랬지. 너무 오래전의 기억이라 잠시 잊고 있었소.”
300|
301|“휴우. 전 또 완전히 잊으신 줄 알고.”
302|
303|“그나저나 이 증표를 갖고 있다는 건…… 이 늙은이를 꼭 필요로 하는 일이 생겼다는 뜻이겠구려.”
304|
305|“예, 맞습니다.”
306|
307|“혹 공자가 모셔 온 여스님에 관한 일이오? 그렇다면 크게 걱정할 필요 없소. 당장 어려운 고비는 넘겼으니.”
308|
309|묘령사태가 누워 있을 모옥을 바라본 신의가 말을 이었다.
310|
311|“비록 순탄하지는 않겠으나…… 남은 치료가 끝난 후 충분히 요양한다면 완쾌할 수 있을 것이오.”

Where had the sudden breeze come from? And where was the bright sunlight pouring in from?

[P79]
Every single thing I saw felt like one of the Seven Wonders of the World.

[P80]
*The pyramids have nothing on this.*

[P81]
There was a place where the seasons changed after only a few steps, so what was so special about the pyramids? Some Egyptian logistics officer had probably run his workers ragged building them.

[P82]
All the pharaoh had to do was put on a solemn face and say, “This pharaoh is disappointed in you,” a few times, and they would start hauling stones while getting whipped.

[P83]
But this place…

[P84]
This was on an entirely different level.

[P85]
“Young Master Jin?”

[P86]
“Huh? Oh, yeah.”

[P87]
“We’re almost there. We only have to cross that hill.”

[P88]
We hurriedly came to our senses and followed Mungyeong again.

[P89]
Once we crossed the low hill covered in green grass, a small thatched hut came into view, standing alone on a flat stretch of land.

[P90]
And…

[P91]
He was there.

[P92]
“Master!”

[P93]
At Mungyeong’s shout, an old man planting something in the vegetable garden before the hut straightened his bent back. His beard was as white as the snow we had seen along the way. His eyes were clear and framed by deep wrinkles.

[P94]
When he noticed us, the corners of his eyes curved gently.

[P95]
“Some honored guests have arrived.”

[P96]
We had finally found him.

[P97]
The Divine Physician.

[P98]
* * *

[P99]
It was a long while before we properly spoke with the Divine Physician.

[P100]
After examining Venerable Myoryeong, the Divine Physician had Mungyeong carry her into the hut. The two of them did not emerge again until a shichen later.

[P101]
“It has been a long time since anyone came to visit.”

[P102]
The Divine Physician’s sudden voice was like a cool spring breeze. I had been pacing around the hut and hurriedly bowed.

[P103]
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan pays his respects to the Divine Physician.”

[P104]
“Dong Feng.”

[P105]
“Pardon?”

[P106]
“That is my name. The title Divine Physician is too grand for me, so please call me Old Man Dong.”

[P107]
How could I call the greatest physician under heaven Old Man Dong, as if he were some old man Kim at a neighborhood real estate office?

[P108]
*I was young enough to be his grandson, too.*

[P109]
But faced with the Divine Physician’s benevolent gaze, I had no choice but to comply.

[P110]
“Yes. I will, Old Man Dong.”

[P111]
“Thank you, Young Master Jin.”

[P112]
The Divine Physician smiled gently, then exchanged greetings with everyone else, one by one.

[P113]
He remained courteous even toward those of us who were far younger than him, and he never once seemed hurried.

[P114]
“Hello! I’m Cheongpung!”

[P115]
He did not even lose his smile in front of the local lunatic.

[P116]
“Heh heh. You’re a very energetic person. My name is Dong Feng. You may call me Old Man Dong, just like the others.”

[P117]
“But my grandfather told me I have to show respect to my elders.”

[P118]
“Your grandfather taught you well. But if our hearts are in accord, what does age matter? Simply think of me as a friend who happens to be a little older.”

[P119]
“A friend?”

[P120]
“That’s right. A friend.”

[P121]
Cheongpung smiled brightly.

[P122]
“Then let’s get along, Old Man Dong!”

[P123]
“Heh heh. Heh heh heh!”

[P124]
He was laughing?

[P125]
Was he some kind of Murim Joker? The type who laughed when he was angry and laughed when he was dumbfounded?

[P126]
“Old Man Dong, have you ever tried candy?”

[P127]
“I’m quite fond of sweets. I used to enjoy candied hawthorn skewers,[^1] too.”

[P128]
“Hey, me too!”

[P129]
The setting looked like a healing movie, but the conversation was pure horror thriller. In the end, Gung Gibang’s face went deathly pale. He clamped both hands over Cheongpung’s mouth and slowly backed away.

[P130]
The Divine Physician laughed heartily at the sight, then turned to Mungyeong.

[P131]
“You have brought some interesting people.”

[P132]
Mungyeong bowed deeply.

[P133]
“I’m sorry, Master. I brought them without your permission.”

[P134]
“No, no. Heaven brings people together through fate. This, too, must be the natural order. Wouldn’t you agree?”

[P135]
His last question was directed at me. I nodded and held out the Divine Physician’s Token I had prepared in advance.

[P136]
“This is a token you left behind long ago, Divine Physician—or rather, Old Man Dong. The Luoyang Strange Physician gave it to me and told me to seek you out.”

[P137]
“I did?”

[P138]
“Pardon?”

[P139]
No way. Had he forgotten?

[P140]
The Divine Physician tilted his head. Only after Mungyeong reminded him again did he let out a small exclamation.

[P141]
“Ah, yes. I remember now. It happened so long ago that it had slipped my mind.”

[P142]
“Whew. For a moment, I thought you’d forgotten completely.”

[P143]
“In any case, if you possess this token… that must mean something has happened that requires this old man’s aid.”

[P144]
“Yes, that’s right.”

[P145]
“Is it about the nun you brought here? If so, there is no need to worry too much. She has already survived the immediate crisis.”

[P146]
The Divine Physician looked toward the hut where Venerable Myoryeong lay and continued.

[P147]
“It will not be an easy road, but… once the rest of her treatment is complete, sufficient rest should allow her to make a full recovery.”

[P148]
It was the best news I had heard in a long time. Not only had Venerable Myoryeong escaped the brink of death, but the Divine Physician truly possessed medical skill worthy of his reputation.

[P149]
I took a deep breath before speaking.

[P150]
“There’s another patient.”

[P151]
“Another patient?”

[P152]
“The man who gave me this token said that only the Divine Physician could treat him.”

[P153]
“Only I can treat him…”

[P154]
The Divine Physician repeated the words quietly, then spoke.

[P155]
“Birth, aging, sickness, and death are not for mere humans to decide. But if there is even the slightest possibility, I will do my utmost as a physician.”

[P156]
“That’s enough… That’s all I need.”

[P157]
There had been a time when my mother was sick.

[P158]
The doctor in charge of her surgery had said the same thing.

[P159]
*I’ll do my best.*

[P160]
For Hayeon and me, those words had been our only hope, and the surgery had been a success.

[P161]
Just as I had done with that doctor in the past, I clasped the Divine Physician’s wrinkled hand.

[P162]
“Please. Old Man Dong.”

[P163]
The Divine Physician smiled benevolently, as though he understood everything.

[P164]
“Let us see the patient first.”

[P165]
After that came nothing but waiting and anxiety.

[P166]
Once Jeok Cheongang, who had been lying on the pack frame, was carried into the hut, I paced back and forth, waiting for the Divine Physician and Mungyeong to emerge.

[P167]
Butterflies and honeybees flitted through the flower field, and fresh green leaves sprouted from the trees, but I felt nothing.

[P168]
*It went well. It must have gone well.*

[P169]
I could not even bring myself to approach the hut, afraid that I might hear something bad.

[P170]
I walked for a long time, endlessly repeating that single thought.

[P171]
Only after the sunlight had faded and a pale darkness settled over the land did I return to the hut.

[P172]
There, the exhausted Divine Physician and Mungyeong were waiting for me with faint smiles.

[P173]
“I believe I can treat him.”

[P174]
The instant I heard those words, all the strength drained from my legs, and a familiar alert pierced my ears.

[P175]
Ding.

[P176]
> **System**
>
> - Quest condition, **Get Examined by the Divine Physician**, completed!
>
> - Quest, **Find Mr. Shin in Sichuan**, successfully completed!

[P177]
[^1]: Candied hawthorn skewers are a traditional snack made by coating fruit in hardened sugar.
```

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 341

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃341화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|며칠 전, 문경과 나누었던 대화가 뇌리를 스쳤다.
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|‘그동안 감사했습니다.’
 10|
 11|‘감사 인사는 무슨. 훌륭한 의원이 되는 것에만 집중해.’
 12|
 13|‘신의처럼요?’
 14|
 15|‘그래, 신의처럼.’
 16|
 17|
 18|
 19|그리고 지나치듯 흘린 마지막 한마디도.
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|‘아쉽지만 이번에는 함께 못 가겠네요. 이만 스승님께 돌아가야 해서요.’
 24|
 25|
 26|
 27|왜 몰랐을까.
 28|
 29|생각해 보면 문경은 처음부터 비범한 구석이 있는 녀석이었다. 수적들에게 목숨을 위협받는 상황에서 발휘한 놀라운 기지, 나이답지 않은 침착성과 뛰어난 의술까지.
 30|
 31|‘그뿐만이 아니야.’
 32|
 33|수적들에 의해 장강 밑바닥으로 가라앉을 뻔한 녀석이 넉살 좋게 쾌조선에 얻어 타지를 않나, 무림에서도 한 성깔 하기로 유명한 사천당문에 고작 약방문을 얻으러 갔다.
 34|
 35|간덩이에 보톡스를 맞은 무림인들도 꺼릴 법한 일들을, 문경은 아무렇지 않게 해 왔다.
 36|
 37|‘게다가 방금 보여 준 말과 행동들은…….’
 38|
 39|문경이 말한 흑수인(黑手印)이 어떤 무공이고 어느 정도의 위력을 지녔는지, 나는 모른다.
 40|
 41|다만 한 가지는 사실은 알겠다.
 42|
 43|“신의. 네가 바로 신의의 제자였어.”
 44|
 45|“……!”
 46|
 47|“……!”
 48|
 49|기쁨과 허탈함이 뒤섞인 내 말을 들은 다른 녀석들이 눈을 크게 뜨고 문경을 바라보았다.
 50|
 51|순간 내려앉은 숨 막히는 적막에 문경이 몸을 움츠렸다.
 52|
 53|“죄, 죄송해요. 하지만 말씀드릴 수 없었어요.”
 54|
 55|“어째서?”
 56|
 57|반사적으로 되묻고도 아차 싶었다. 일평생 정체를 숨기며 살아온 신의다. 그 제자인 문경이 입을 다문 것은 당연했다.
 58|
 59|아마도 묘령사태의 목숨이 경각에 달리지 않았다면, 녀석은 끝끝내 스승의 정체를 발설하지 않았을 것이 분명했다.
 60|
 61|“신의는, 아니 네 스승님께서는 지금 어디 계시지?”
 62|
 63|머뭇거리던 문경이 입술을 꼭 깨물었다.
 64|
 65|“그 전에, 한 가지만 약속해 주실 수 있나요?”
 66|
 67|“비밀은 지킨다. 반드시.”
 68|
 69|나는 단호한 대답과 함께 품에서 뭔가를 꺼내 보여 주었다.
 70|
 71|그건 요즘 들어 틈만 나면 인벤토리에서 꺼내 들여다보는 물건이었다.
 72|
 73|
 74|
 75|[오배자(五倍子)는 사천 땅에서 나는 것이 제일이오.]
 76|
 77|
 78|
 79|옥빛 사금파리에 적힌 희미한 글씨를 본 문경의 눈이 커다래졌다.
 80|
 81|“이건…….”
 82|
 83|“알아보겠어?”
 84|
 85|“네, 틀림없이 스승님의 필체인걸요.”
 86|
 87|신기한 듯 [신의의 증표]를 요모조모 살피던 문경이 아, 하고 탄성을 흘렸다.
 88|
 89|“그러고 보니 언젠가 스승님께서 그러셨어요. 아주 오래전, 어느 명의에게 사천으로 찾아오라는 증표를 남기신 적이 있다고. 그런데 어찌 이것을 공자님께서…….”
 90|
 91|“그 명의에게 직접 건네받았어. 신의가 아니면 치료할 수 없는 환자가 있거든.”
 92|
 93|나는 힘주어 말을 이었다.
 94|
 95|“반드시 살려야 하는 사람이야.”
 96|
 97|“어디의 누구신지는 모르나…… 공자님께서는 그분을 소중하게 여기시는군요.”
 98|
 99|소중한 사람이라.
100|
101|그래, 그런 것 같다. 내게 있어 적천강은 소중한 사람이다. 그는 나를 위해 모든 것을 내어 주었고, 이제는 내가 그를 지킬 차례다.
102|
103|“응. 맞아.”
104|
105|문경은 희미하게 웃으며 고개를 끄덕였다.
106|
107|“따라오세요. 스승님께 안내해 드릴게요.”
108|
109|
110|
111|* * *
112|
113|
114|
115|뽀득, 뽀드득.
116|
117|쌓인 눈이 걸음을 옮길 때마다 뭉개졌다.
118|
119|나는 주위를 둘러봤다. 서리 낀 앙상한 나뭇가지. 시선이 닿는 곳마다 소복하게 쌓인 새하얀 눈.
120|
121|‘봐도 봐도 신기하네.’
122|
123|밖은 새싹이 고개를 내미는 초봄인데, 지금 우리가 걷고 있는 곳은 눈 내린 어느 겨울날의 풍경이다.
124|
125|‘이게 바로 기문진(奇門陣)…….’
126|
127|신의에게 안내해 주겠다며 문경이 향한 곳은, 앞서 청성파와 함께 수색하던 바로 그 산이었다. 하지만 어느 지점에 이르러 그가 몇 개의 바위를 낑낑거리며 옮기니 새로운 길과 풍경이 펼쳐지는 것이 아닌가.
128|
129|‘난생처음 보는 광경에 나를 포함한 모두의 입이 딱 벌어졌었지.’
130|
131|문경은 이걸 설치해 준 사람이 기환노사(奇幻老師)라고 말해 줬다.
132|
133|궁기방이 침까지 튀겨 가며 설명한 바로는, 기환노사는 까마득한 과거에 천하제일의 진법가라 불리던 인물이라고 했다.
134|
135|그가 신의와 어떤 인연이 있었는지는 모르겠지만 이런 걸 설치해 놓다니. 하마터면 코앞에 두고 한참을 헤맬 뻔했다.
136|
137|‘이러니까 아무도 못 찾지.’
138|
139|날고 긴다는 무림인과 수많은 관군을 풀어놓으면 뭐 하나.
140|
141|정석대로 산 하나하나를 뒤졌다면 반년이 아니라 반세기로도 시간이 부족했을 것이다.
142|
143|“와아, 와아아!”
144|
145|눈밭에 풀어놓은 강아지처럼 몇 발짝 앞에서 뛰어가던 청풍이 탄성을 내질렀다. 뭐라 핀잔을 주려던 나도 다음 순간 완전히 뒤바뀐 광경에 입을 딱 벌렸다.
146|
147|“……와, 씨. 뭐냐 이거.”
148|
149|고작 몇 걸음 만에 또 세상이 바뀌었다.
150|
151|눈으로 온통 새하얗던 한겨울의 풍경이 아닌 완연한 봄으로.
152|
153|사방이 온통 푸르렀고 이름 모를 꽃들이 활짝 만개해 있었다. 넋 나간 얼굴로 다가온 혁무진이 물었다.
154|
155|“조장님. 지금 제가 헛것을 보고 있는 겁니까?”
156|
157|“나도 몰라, 인마.”
158|
159|우리 중 가장 무림 경험이 풍부한 궁기방조차도 멍하니 입을 벌린 채 중얼거렸다.
160|
161|“허어…… 헙! 퉷퉷! 이거 뭐야!”
162|
163|“나비?”
164|
165|세상에, 진짜 나비네. 그것도 한두 마리가 아니다.
166|
167|형형색색(形形色色).
168|
169|꽃밭 곳곳에 앉아 있던 수백 마리의 나비가 동시에 날아오르는 모습은 장관 그 자체였다.
170|
171|쏴아아아아.
172|
173|때마침 불어오는 바람은 어디에서 왔는지, 환하게 내리쬐는 햇살은 또 어디서 들어오는지.
174|
175|내게는 지금 보이는 하나하나가 7대 불가사의였다.
176|
177|‘여기에 비하면 피라미드는 아무것도 아니네.’
178|
179|몇 걸음 차이로 계절이 바뀌는 곳도 있는데 피라미드가 대수냐. 이집트 행정 보급관이 애들 굴려서 지었겠지 뭐.
180|
181|파라오가 근엄한 얼굴로 본 파라오는 너희에게 실망했다, 몇 번 날려 주면 채찍 맞으면서 돌 나르게 되어 있다.
182|
183|하지만 이곳은…… 완전히 다른 영역이다.
184|
185|“진 공자님?”
186|
187|“어? 어, 응.”
188|
189|“거의 다 도착했어요. 이제 저 언덕만 넘어가면 됩니다.”
190|

- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
